content:
Apple TV streaming service focuses on original content and has been enriching its exclusive series and film lineup over the years. Apple recently added another batch of classic films to the service, available for subscribers to stream at no extra cost.

It is not yet clear whether this new measure is permanent or a limited-time promotion. The service ran a similar campaign a few years ago, but it lasted only a short while.

You can find the current lineup in the newly launched "Great Movies Available Now on Apple TV" carousel within the Apple TV app.

The available selections vary slightly by region. So far, the content is known to be offered in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. The free-to-watch film list for the U.S. region includes:

  • The Martian
  • Arrival
  • The Bourne Identity
  • Tenet
  • E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
  • The Big Sick
  • I, Robot
  • Forgetting Sarah Marshall
  • The Faculty
  • The Sixth Sense
  • Prisoners
  • The Other Guys
  • The Notebook
  • The Lord of the Rings Trilogy
  • Titanic
  • Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol
  • A Beautiful Mind
  • The Aviator
  • Police Story

These films previously had to be purchased or rented from the Apple TV store, and are now marked as "Just Added," available for free streaming to Apple TV subscribers. New accounts can enjoy a seven-day free trial. The service normally costs US$12.99 per month, or US$99 per year. Apple TV can also be accessed through the Apple One bundle subscription plan.

Streaming is available via native TV apps on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Android, Windows, and other devices, or through the browser at tv.apple.com.

This new batch of classic films will further enrich the existing library of over 300 original titles; please refer to our full guide for a complete list of available streaming titles. However, compared with films, Apple TV appears to have achieved greater success with its original series.

The next original film will be Mayday, an action comedy starring Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh, scheduled to premiere in September.
